added_failures_source.note: derived by parsing the pytest short-summary FAILED lines from the two logs the reviewed manifest names; both logs declare 0 failures (base 56 passed / after 69 passed) so the added set is empty. Controls in the reviewing run's logs/derive.log falsify the instrument: an injected head-only failure is seen as 1 added id, the same id present in both logs is not counted as added, and an absent head log reads as None rather than 0.

call_sites: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4573 the dispatch writes worker_scratch_dir(run_id) onto the run's pointer as "scratch", the record every later removal reads
reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5477 _removable_scratch_target holds every check the removal depends on
reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5515 remove_worker_scratch removes through it and prints the path it removed
reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5570 _worker_runtime_environment sets the worker's TMPDIR to ensure_worker_scratch(run_id), reached by every launch and resume path
reckon/crew/promotion.py:3529 the release fallback, which never raises and reports the reason instead
reckon/crew/promotion.py:3646 _release_run_workspace, the shared release step promotion and discard both funnel through

findings.text: The _removable_scratch_target docstring says a recorded path's value is "resilience to a root that moved", but the check at :5509 requires the resolved parent to be the current resolved scratch root, so a root that moved makes the record foreign and it is withheld rather than used. My probe moved RECKON_WORKER_SCRATCH_ROOT from root-a to root-b between the create and the remove and measured removed=False, scratch_withheld='scratch path is not the directory this run owns', the root-a scratch surviving on disk and the root-b directory left untouched (log logs/root_moved.log of the reviewing run). The behaviour is the safe direction — it refuses a directory the check cannot vouch for, reports the reason in the release result, and the derived path still removes normally (same probe, control-derived removed=True) — so this is a claim in the docstring and in 1cf126c7's message that the code no longer delivers as cleanup, not a wrong removal. In production exposure is narrow because the root is a constant unless RECKON_WORKER_SCRATCH_ROOT is overridden differently between dispatch and release.

item_verdicts.goal: All five properties hold at bff857cd. remove_worker_scratch resolves its target through _removable_scratch_target, which refuses a final component that is not the validated run id (:5509), a resolved parent other than the resolved scratch root (:5509), and a symlink checked before the resolve so a link is never followed (:5502). My probe under a synthesised root withheld all of: a sibling run's directory, a symlink to a sibling, a symlink pointing outside the root, a directory outside the root, the root itself, a same-named directory one level deeper, a relative sibling path and a dangling symlink, with the target surviving in every case; the two positive controls (the recorded path naming the run's own directory, and the derived path) each removed the directory and printed it, so the guard is not a blanket refusal. The declared mutation reddens the sibling case as claimed, and the evidence fragment and its figure are absent from the tree at bff857cd while present at 1dfda944, with the content kept in the run directory's record/.

justifications.durability: The sibling-survival property is load-bearing rather than incidental: under the declared recorded-path mutation the file reddens exactly test_a_recorded_path_naming_a_sibling_is_withheld, and I reinstated the pre-repair check in the same tree and measured the sibling deleted (removed=True, sibling_survives=False) against the repaired guard's withholding (removed=False, sibling_survives=True) with the patch restored afterwards, so the pair isolates the repair rather than the scenario.
justifications.evidence: after.log names revision bff857cd, its tree, module and cwd and 69 passed; base.log names 40d23d9 in a scratch tree and 56 passed; my independent re-run of the same 11-file arm in a separate scratch tree at bff857cd reproduced 69 passed in 174s, and my derivation over the two logs returns 0 added ids with controls that see an injected id, ignore one present in both logs, and read an absent head log as unmeasured; both declared negative controls reproduce their declared first line verbatim and the promised red sets.
justifications.fit: The repair extracts _removable_scratch_target so every check applies whatever path a caller offers, the symlink check is placed before the resolve with the reason stated, the run-id refusal names the mechanism rather than a stage, and the new test file is formatted and at 0 ruff findings while dispatch.py is 7=7 and promotion.py 10=10 by concurrent finding count, with no reformat hunk touching the node's new identifiers. One deduction: the docstring at :5487 claims the recorded path's value is resilience to a root that moved, and the measured behaviour withholds instead of removing when the root has moved.
